title: How Your Habits Shape Your Identity (and Vice Versa)
coreMove: Convert each repetition into a vote for the identity you want to make believable.
sourcePressure: Habits shape identity by turning repeated action into evidence for a self-concept, and identity-based change lasts longer than outcome-only chasing.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating identity as an affirmation instead of evidence earned by repeated behavior.

hook: starting with a definition of identity-based habits
counterintuition: the problem is not motivation alone

exampleSpecs.domain: a community choir member becoming the person who arrives early to tune chairs
exampleSpecs.audience: an amateur singer who wants to believe she belongs
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the identity of reliable member forms before her solo confidence does
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she writes her name on the setup roster for the fourth Thursday and sees the role become harder to deny
exampleSpecs.firstImage: stacked folding chairs under a church balcony

exampleSpecs.domain: a diabetic teen choosing lunch by asking what a careful athlete would pack
exampleSpecs.audience: a school nurse coaching a student tired of lectures
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether food choices become identity evidence instead of punishment
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he swaps the vending-machine pastry for the lunch he packed after naming the vote it casts
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a cafeteria tray paused under a heat lamp

exampleSpecs.domain: a new library volunteer shelving returns every Tuesday without being asked
exampleSpecs.audience: a retiree rebuilding civic identity after moving towns
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a tiny repeated contribution becomes proof of belonging
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she notices staff stop asking if she is visiting and start handing her the return cart
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a blue return cart with date-stamped paperbacks

exampleSpecs.domain: a junior firefighter checking breathing gear after every drill
exampleSpecs.audience: a recruit who wants respect from veterans
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether identity forms through unglamorous checks rather than speeches
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he repeats the mask seal check after everyone leaves and logs it as the kind of firefighter he is becoming
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a wet turnout coat hanging beside an open gear locker

exampleSpecs.domain: a graduate student voting for the identity of researcher by submitting messy notes
exampleSpecs.audience: a first-year scholar stuck polishing outlines
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether she becomes a working researcher before feeling brilliant
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: her advisor asks what evidence a researcher would create today and she uploads three rough observations
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a lab notebook with a torn corner beside an upload portal

exampleSpecs.domain: a father learning to be the calm pickup parent through one repeated doorway pause
exampleSpecs.audience: a parent whose temper spikes after commute traffic
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether identity changes through visible votes before the child trusts it
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he stops with his hand on the daycare gate latch, takes one breath, and enters as the patient version for the twelfth time
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a metal daycare gate shining in rain

skillTargets: identify which identity a repeated action reinforces
replace outcome-only goals with evidence-building reps

tryThisNowSpec: Before the next small action, finish this sentence on paper: A person who does this is the kind of person who _____. Then do one vote for that identity.
